subject: geography
title: The Double Burden: Undernutrition and Obesity
welcome_lead: Many countries face hunger and obesity at the same time — even within the same households.
meta_desc: Geography Adventure: double burden of malnutrition, nutrition transition and policy responses.
final_note: You have seen the paradox of malnutrition. Healthy food systems must address both ends of the spectrum.

concepts.def: Insufficient intake of energy or essential nutrients, leading to stunting, wasting or micronutrient deficiencies.
Excess intake of calories, particularly from ultra-processed foods, leading to overweight and obesity.
Coexistence of undernutrition and overnutrition in the same population, household or individual.
Body Mass Index = mass(kg) / height(m)²; overweight ≥ 25, obese ≥ 30.
Low height-for-age caused by chronic undernutrition, especially in early childhood.
Shift from traditional diets toward energy-dense, processed foods as countries urbanise and incomes rise.

walkthroughs.body_html: The WHO and FAO note that nearly 150 million children under 5 are stunted while over 1.9 billion adults are overweight, including 650 million obese. Many MICs (Mexico, South Africa) face both crises simultaneously, sometimes within the same family.

The nutrition transition (Popkin) describes how diets shift toward sugars, fats and processed foods. Aggressive marketing, urbanisation, sedentary lifestyles and food deserts compound the shift. Climate stress on staple crops increases reliance on cheap, energy-dense alternatives.

Mexico's tax on sugary drinks (2014), Chile's front-of-pack warning labels and the UK's sugar levy on soft drinks illustrate policy responses. Programmes also target nutrition-sensitive agriculture, biofortification (e.g. vitamin A-enriched 'Golden Rice') and school meals.
